texts.title: The Voyager Program
texts.clean_text: The Voyager program is a pair of robotic probes launched by NASA in 1977 to study the outer Solar System. Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 were built at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory in California. Voyager 2 lifted off first, on 20 August 1977, and Voyager 1 followed on 5 September 1977 along a faster path. Voyager 1 flew past Jupiter in 1979 and Saturn in 1980, returning the first detailed images of their moons. Voyager 2 remains the only spacecraft to have visited Uranus and Neptune, which it reached in 1986 and 1989. Each probe carries a Golden Record, a phonograph disc holding sounds and pictures chosen to portray the diversity of life on Earth. The contents of the records were selected by a committee led by the astronomer Carl Sagan. The records were not meant to be recovered; they were intended as a message to any intelligent life that might one day find them. In 2012 Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause and entered interstellar space, the first human-made object to do so. The probes are powered by radioisotope generators, not solar panels, because sunlight is far too weak in the outer Solar System. NASA still receives faint signals from both spacecraft today.

texts.title: The Great Barrier Reef
texts.clean_text: The Great Barrier Reef is the world's largest coral reef system, stretching more than 2,300 kilometres along the north-east coast of Australia. It is composed of nearly 3,000 individual reefs and around 900 islands. The reef is not a single organism but a vast structure built by billions of tiny animals called coral polyps. It can be seen from low Earth orbit and is often described as the largest living structure on the planet. In 1981 the reef was designated a World Heritage Site by UNESCO. The area supports an extraordinary diversity of life, including more than 1,500 species of fish and six of the world's seven species of marine turtle. Rising sea temperatures have caused several mass bleaching events, in which stressed corals expel the algae that give them colour and energy. The reef is managed by the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority, which was established in 1975. Tourism brings billions of dollars to the regional economy each year, but it also adds pressure to an already fragile ecosystem. Scientists warn that the reef will not survive unchecked warming.

hybrid_rrf.label: Hybrid RRF
hybrid_rrf.desc: Reciprocal-rank fusion of SPLADE and ColBERT. Strongest retriever in this example.

splade_v3.label: SPLADE v3
splade_v3.desc: Learned sparse retriever with term expansion.

bm25.label: BM25
bm25.desc: Classic lexical baseline over word unigrams.

extract_fact.label: Extract fact
extract_fact.desc: The answer is stated explicitly in the passage.

inference.label: Inference
inference.desc: The answer requires combining or negating stated facts.

numeric.label: Numeric reasoning
numeric.desc: The answer hinges on a quantity or measurement.

multi_hop.label: Multi-hop
multi_hop.desc: The answer requires linking facts across sentences.

open_corpus.label: Open-corpus
open_corpus.desc: Retrieval runs over all texts, so it can surface passages from the wrong article.

text_restricted.label: Text-restricted
text_restricted.desc: Retrieval is limited to chunks from the correct source text.

closed_book.label: Closed-book
closed_book.desc: The model answers from its own parameters, with no text provided.

full_text_oracle.label: Full-text oracle
full_text_oracle.desc: The model is given the entire correct source text. An upper bound.

rag_text_restricted.label: RAG (text-restricted)
rag_text_restricted.desc: Retrieval limited to the correct text, then the model answers.

rag_open_corpus.label: RAG (open-corpus)
rag_open_corpus.desc: Retrieval over the whole corpus, then the model answers. The realistic setting.

critical_only.label: Critical only
critical_only.desc: The retriever surfaced the evidence for the correct answer, and no distractor.

both.label: Critical + distractor
both.desc: The retriever surfaced both the correct evidence and a distractor.

distractor_only.label: Distractor only
distractor_only.desc: The retriever surfaced a distractor but missed the correct evidence. The trap.

neither.label: Neither
neither.desc: The retriever surfaced neither the correct evidence nor a distractor.

1.label: Named entities
1.desc: People, organisations and places. Fine-tuned encoder taggers score highest.

2.label: Quantities & time
2.desc: Numbers, measurements and dates. Encoders and LLMs are close.

3.label: Discourse phenomena
3.desc: Negation and coreference. Large LLM taggers keep a clear edge.

ent-gpe.label: Place (GPE)
ent-gpe.desc: A geopolitical entity: country, region, or landmark.

temporal.label: Temporal expression
temporal.desc: A date, year, or time expression.

negation.label: Negation cue
negation.desc: A word or phrase that negates or reverses a proposition.

coref.label: Coreference
coref.desc: A pronoun or reference whose antecedent must be resolved.

items.label: Named entities
items.note: (people, organisations, places): recovered by the encoder taggers, missed by the LLMs.

items.label: Discourse phenomena
items.note: (e.g. negation and coreference): recovered by the LLM taggers, missed by the encoders.

intro.title: Example dataset: MiniWiki-EN
intro.tagline: The same workbench, a completely different study — English encyclopedia text, other retrievers, other LLMs, an entity-and-discourse tagging task.
paragraphs: This is the downloadable example bundle. It shares nothing with the Luxembourgish reference dataset except the JSON schema: different language, different retrievers (BM25, SPLADE v3, ColBERT v2, E5-large-v2, hybrid RRF), different QA models (GPT-4o, Llama 3.1 405B, Mistral Large 2, Qwen 2.5 72B), and a different annotation taxonomy (named entities and discourse phenomena tagged by spaCy, Stanza and Flair versus GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet prompted for tagging).
Every panel you see is rendered purely from this file. That is the point: the interface is a reusable shell for evidence-grounded diagnostic studies, not a viewer hardwired to one corpus.
how_to_read: Pick a question on the left; the passage and all four panels re-render on it.
Green marks the evidence for the correct answer, red marks a distractor.
Switch tabs to see retrieval, model answers, the retrieval-trap chart, and the annotation matrix.

about.intro: This example is a data-driven instantiation of the same shell. It renders whatever lives in the uploaded bundle against a fixed JSON schema, so any study that shares one character-offset coordinate system over its texts gets the same four linked panels. MiniWiki-EN is a deliberately different instantiation from the Luxembourgish reference.
reuse: Upload a bundle of your own study outputs and watch every panel re-render on it, or replace the files in public/data/ for a permanent deployment.
Every layer indexes into each text's clean_text, so a retrieved chunk, an evidence span, and an annotated token all speak the same coordinates.
Nothing in the interface is specific to any one language, model set, or label set — this English example is the proof.

schema.desc: The source passages. Each clean_text defines the shared coordinate system.
MCQs with gold answers and critical/distractor character spans.
One record per question x model x setting, with the retrieval-trap class.
Per (text, category) gold occurrences and each tagger's surface predictions.
Corpus-level curves, trap classes, and per-category / aggregate F1.
The vocabularies: retrievers, models, annotators, categories, regimes, settings.
Per-question ranked chunks per retriever x scope.
